Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Keep the supplied language.", "input": "The North Quay Chess Association opened registration for its annual Harbor Lantern Open on Monday, March 4. The tournament will take place at the Alder Street Community Hall on May 18 and 19, with five rounds scheduled across the weekend. Organizers expect players from nearby counties as well as residents of the city, and the hall’s main room can hold 96 competitors. Registration closes on May 10, unless all places are filled earlier. The association has reserved a smaller room for analysis, quiet breaks, and parents accompanying junior players.

This year’s event is rated by the national chess federation and is open to players with current membership. A player whose membership has lapsed may renew through the federation before the first round, but the tournament desk cannot process renewals. The entry form asks for each player’s full name, federation identification number, rating, club if applicable, and a contact email address. Players without a federation rating may enter as unrated. Organizers have asked entrants to check their identification numbers carefully, since an incorrect number can attach a result to the wrong player’s record.

The registration page lists two sections. The Open Section has no rating ceiling, while the U1600 Section is limited to players rated below 1600 on the May rating list. Players may register for only one section. If an entrant’s rating changes before the list is published, the tournament director will use the published May rating to determine eligibility for U1600. Unrated players may request placement in that section, but the director will review the request before confirming it. The entry fee is £32 for the Open and £26 for U1600, with a £5 discount for juniors under eighteen.

1. To complete an entry, players should submit the online form and pay by card or bank transfer. The form sends an automatic receipt, but that receipt is not a confirmation that a place has been reserved. The registrar will check the details and send a separate confirmation email, usually within two working days. Bank transfers should include the player’s surname and federation number in the payment reference. Cash and cheques will not be accepted at the venue, and the desk will not hold a place while waiting for payment.

A player who needs to withdraw should email the registrar rather than replying to the automated receipt. Withdrawals received by May 10 will receive a refund minus a £4 administration charge. After that date, refunds are available only if the organizers can fill the place from the waiting list. The waiting list will be kept in order of completed registration, not by rating or club. If a place becomes available, the registrar will contact the next player and allow 24 hours for a response before moving to the next name.

The schedule gives players time to check in before the first round. Doors open at 9:00 a.m. on Saturday, and the opening announcement is planned for 10:15. Round one begins at 10:30, followed by rounds at 1:30 and 4:00. On Sunday, rounds four and five are scheduled for 10:00 and 1:00, with prize presentations expected at about 4:00. The timetable may shift slightly if a round runs long, but the organizers will post any changes on the noticeboard beside the tournament desk.

Players should bring a chess set and a clock if they have them. The association will provide equipment at boards where a player has not brought a set, but it cannot guarantee a particular style of clock. Standard federation rules apply, including the requirement to record moves unless an arbiter instructs otherwise. Phones must be switched off during play. A player who needs an adjustment for access, seating, or a medical reason can contact the registrar in advance; requests will be handled privately, and the organizers will discuss what the venue can provide.

The hall is about a ten-minute walk from North Quay station, and the number 6 bus stops on Alder Street. Limited free parking is available behind the building, but spaces are shared with the Saturday market and cannot be reserved. The association recommends allowing extra time for travel and check-in. Water will be available in the main room, while a café across the road plans to open during both days. Players may bring their own food, but the hall asks visitors not to eat at the chess tables.

When the committee reviewed the registration page, volunteer coordinator Mina Shah said, “People usually have the right information, but one missing digit in a federation number can create a lot of work later.” The registrar has therefore added a final review screen before payment and will compare submitted names against the federation list where possible. This check may take longer for players who have recently changed clubs or surnames, so those entrants are encouraged to include a note with their form. The committee will not publish email addresses or phone numbers in the event materials.

The association will post the confirmed player list and round pairings on its website after check-in closes, and printed pairings will also be displayed in the hall. Results will be submitted to the federation after the tournament and may take several days to appear in individual rating records. The organizers are still looking for two volunteers to help with the refreshment table on Sunday; interested members can contact Mina Shah.
